comparators.definition: The fixed Noisy Power Method returns a width-$b_{\mathrm{blk}}$ subspace approximately containing the true leading $k$-dimensional singular subspace. The base error $\|(I-X_LX_L^{\mathsf T})U\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ must not exceed $\varepsilon$. It measures how well the output contains the target subspace.

domains.definition: Return the fixed algorithm’s final orthogonal block $X_L$ with $b_{\mathrm{blk}}$ columns. Compression to rank k is not required.

objects.definition: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, $\sigma_1(A)\le\Lambda$, and $\sigma_k(A)-\sigma_{k+1}(A)\ge g>0$. Let $U\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}$ be an orthonormal basis for the leading singular subspace, with $1\le k\le b_{\mathrm{blk}}\le d$; append zero singular values at the end when needed.
The matrix $U\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}$ is any orthonormal basis for the leading k singular directions of $A$, with $U^{\mathsf T}U=I_k$. The assumed gap makes this subspace unique.
The tuple $(d,k,b_{\rm blk},\Lambda,g,\nu_{\rm tot},\nu_\parallel,\varepsilon,\delta)$ is public.
